content.text: {"cases":[{"id":"C1","instrument_review":"One 70% run on 100 grid puzzles with exact-grid scoring supports a narrow comparison of performance on these puzzles. The report does not say whether runs were repeated, so score consistency is undocumented.","probes":[{"id":"repeat_test","label":"Not established","quote":"The report does not say whether runs were repeated.","reason":"Repetition is neither confirmed nor ruled out."},{"id":"stable","label":"Not established","quote":"The tested system scored 70% in one reported run.","reason":"A single run gives no evidence on stability."}]},{"id":"C2","instrument_review":"A single run is explicitly stated. The 70% score is a one-time result, and consistency across runs was not examined.","probes":[{"id":"repeat_test","label":"Contradicted","quote":"they ran the evaluation exactly once and did not repeat it","reason":"Developers explicitly did not repeat the evaluation."},{"id":"stable","label":"Not established","quote":"ran the evaluation exactly once","reason":"With no repeats, stability cannot be supported; it is not shown to be unstable either."}]},{"id":"C3","instrument_review":"Ten repeats under identical conditions gave 69-71%, a 2-point range that meets the report's own stability definition. This supports stability for this system and setup only, not other claims.","probes":[{"id":"repeat_test","label":"Supported","quote":"repeated the evaluation ten times with the same system, inputs, instructions, resources, and settings","reason":"Repeated same-condition runs were conducted and score variation was recorded."},{"id":"stable","label":"Supported","quote":"Scores ranged from 69% to 71%.","reason":"The range is within the stated two-point definition of stable."}]},{"id":"C4","instrument_review":"Ten identical-condition repeats were run, but scores ranged 20-90%, far outside the report's two-point stability rule. The single 70% result is therefore unreliable.","probes":[{"id":"repeat_test","label":"Supported","quote":"repeated the evaluation ten times with the same system, inputs, instructions, resources, and settings","reason":"Repeat testing was done and variation recorded."},{"id":"stable","label":"Contradicted","quote":"Scores ranged from 20% to 90%.","reason":"A 70-point range violates the at-most-two-point definition."}]},{"id":"C5","instrument_review":"Installation instructions add usability information but no evaluation evidence. Repetition and consistency remain undocumented, as in the single-run case.","probes":[{"id":"repeat_test","label":"Not established","quote":"The report does not say whether runs were repeated.","reason":"Installation instructions do not address repetition."},{"id":"stable","label":"Not established","quote":"They report no additional evaluation results.","reason":"No evidence about stability is provided."}]},{"id":"C6","instrument_review":"80 vs 60 solved on the same fixed-instruction puzzles supports a narrow comparison matching the intended use. Nothing supports claims about general intelligence or other tasks. Uncertainty and repeats are not reported.","probes":[{"id":"narrow","label":"Supported","quote":"System A solves 80 puzzles and system B solves 60","reason":"The reported results show A ahead on the evaluated puzzles under fixed conditions."},{"id":"broad","label":"Not established","quote":"Only grid puzzles were tested; no findings about other tasks are supplied.","reason":"No evidence supports a cross-domain claim."}]},{"id":"C7","instrument_review":"The results support only the narrow grid-puzzle comparison. The intended use, selecting by general intelligence across domains, outruns the evidence, so the benchmark is not shown to fit that use.","probes":[{"id":"narrow","label":"Supported","quote":"System A solves 80 puzzles and system B solves 60","reason":"A outperformed B on the evaluated puzzles."},{"id":"broad","label":"Not established","quote":"Only grid puzzles were tested; no findings about other tasks are supplied.","reason":"Evidence is limited to grid puzzles; the broad claim is unsupported."}]},{"id":"C8","instrument_review":"Test scores alone were an insufficient basis for real-world claims. The later randomized, preregistered, blinded trial supports correctness differences in this workshop with an interval excluding zero (12 to 28 points). It did not measure time or safety, and generalization beyond this workshop is untested.","probes":[{"id":"before","label":"Not established","quote":"Initially, only test scores were available.","reason":"Scores alone say nothing about real workshop decisions with assistance."},{"id":"after","label":"Supported","quote":"With A, 90% of decisions were correct; with B, 70%.","reason":"Randomized, blinded trial with an interval of 12 to 28 points supports A for correctness in this workshop."},{"id":"safety","label":"Not established","quote":"Time and safety outcomes were not measured.","reason":"Safety was not assessed, so no safety claim follows."}]},{"id":"P1A","instrument_review":"A single headline score of 75% is given with task and scoring description but no execution history. Neither stability nor instability can be judged.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Not established","quote":"gives no execution history","reason":"No information on repeated evaluations."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Not established","quote":"one headline score of 75%","reason":"One score cannot demonstrate instability."}]},{"id":"P1B","instrument_review":"The record confirms a single evaluation, so score consistency was never measured. Instability is not shown either.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Contradicted","quote":"no repeat evaluations were conducted","reason":"Without repeats, changes could not be measured."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Not established","quote":"this was the only evaluation performed","reason":"One run provides no evidence of instability."}]},{"id":"P2A","instrument_review":"Six identical-condition runs gave scores of 73-75, a 2-point range within the 3-point rule. This supports stability for this AI and setup.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Supported","quote":"identical inputs, settings and resources on six occasions","reason":"Repeated same-condition evaluations are described."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Contradicted","quote":"73, 74, 74, 75, 74 and 73 percent","reason":"The range of 2 points is within the 3-point limit, so the rule is met."}]},{"id":"P2B","instrument_review":"Six identical-condition runs gave scores of 51-82, a 31-point range far exceeding the 3-point stability rule, so scores are unstable.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Supported","quote":"identical inputs, settings and resources on six occasions","reason":"Repeated same-condition evaluations were conducted."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Supported","quote":"51, 66, 79, 55, 82 and 62 percent","reason":"The range of 31 points exceeds the 3-point maximum."}]},{"id":"P3A","instrument_review":"The document covers topics and mark calculation only. It offers no evidence on repeat evaluations or on answer errors.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Not established","quote":"It gives no execution history","reason":"No repeated evaluations are documented."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Not established","quote":"no findings about mistakes in the provided answers","reason":"No findings about mistakes are supplied; their presence or absence is unknown."}]},{"id":"P3B","instrument_review":"The appendix adds installation details only, not evaluation evidence. Consistency and answer correctness remain undocumented.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Not established","quote":"It reports no further evaluation results or examination of answers.","reason":"Appendix adds no repeat-evaluation evidence."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Not established","quote":"no further evaluation results or examination of answers","reason":"No mistakes are demonstrated."}]},{"id":"P4A","instrument_review":"Two editors independently examined all questions and answers, which is a documented review process. But the report gives no agreement count, no error findings and no remaining-error count, so correctness of the release is not shown.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Supported","quote":"Two editors independently examined every question and supplied answer before release.","reason":"Both questions and answers were checked during development."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Not established","quote":"The report does not state whether mistakes were found or how many remained.","reason":"Review does not prove all answers correct."}]},{"id":"P4B","instrument_review":"Editors examined everything, but the report itself identifies twelve wrong answers in the released version, a documented quality problem. Agreement before reconciliation is not reported.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Supported","quote":"Two editors independently examined every question and supplied answer before release.","reason":"Both questions and answers were examined."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Contradicted","quote":"identifies twelve supplied answers as wrong in the released version","reason":"Twelve wrong answers means not every answer is correct."}]},{"id":"P5A","instrument_review":"A fixed software rule gives consistent marks, but consistency is not validity. No comparison with independent correct marks is reported, so marking correctness is unestablished.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Contradicted","quote":"No comparison of those marks with independently established correct marks is reported.","reason":"The passage reports no such test."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Not established","quote":"identical text always receives the same mark","reason":"Consistency does not show correctness for all responses."}]},{"id":"P5B","instrument_review":"Marking is deterministic, and a check against independent marks on 20 chosen responses found two differences, unresolved. This shows a documented problem and limited coverage; correctness is not established.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Supported","quote":"tested the software against independently established correct marks for 20 chosen responses","reason":"Such a test is described."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Contradicted","quote":"Two marks differed and the discrepancies remain unresolved.","reason":"Unresolved mismatches conflict with correct scoring for every response."}]},{"id":"P6A","instrument_review":"A solved 36 and B 24 of 48 under fixed conditions. The stated use is limited to this evaluation, so the findings fit it. No generalization or repeat information is claimed.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Supported","quote":"identifying which system solved more of these 48 grid problems in this evaluation","reason":"The results directly answer the narrow stated use."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Supported","quote":"A solves 36 and B solves 24.","reason":"A solved more problems."}]},{"id":"P6B","instrument_review":"The grid results show A ahead on these problems, but the stated use (general intelligence across subjects and real-world settings) goes far beyond the evidence, since no other tasks or settings are supplied.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Not established","quote":"No results from other tasks or settings are supplied.","reason":"Evidence does not cover the broad stated use."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Supported","quote":"A solves 36 and B solves 24.","reason":"A solved more of the evaluated problems."}]},{"id":"P7A","instrument_review":"The all-or-nothing rule matches the requirement to count only completely correct grids; zero for partial grids is intended. Scoring is aligned with the stated requirement.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Supported","quote":"count only completely correct output grids","reason":"The rule awards points exactly for complete correctness."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Contradicted","quote":"partial correctness is deliberately outside this comparison","reason":"Zero for partial grids is consistent with the requirement."}]},{"id":"P7B","instrument_review":"The rule gives zero to partial grids, but the requirement is credit for each correct cell. This is a documented scoring mismatch.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Contradicted","quote":"give a response credit for every correctly completed cell","reason":"All-or-nothing scoring does not give cell-level credit."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Supported","quote":"A partially correct grid receives zero.","reason":"This conflicts with the requirement to credit partial grids."}]},{"id":"P8A","instrument_review":"Instruction wording varied across evaluations while other factors were fixed, so the design addresses instruction sensitivity, not identical-condition repeatability.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Contradicted","quote":"No evaluation repeats an identical instruction.","reason":"Conditions were not identical across evaluations."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Supported","quote":"each evaluation uses a differently worded instruction","reason":"Instruction wording was varied while other factors were fixed, so score changes reflect instruction changes."}]},{"id":"P8B","instrument_review":"All conditions are identical across evaluations, so the study addresses repeat consistency, not sensitivity to instruction or presentation.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Supported","quote":"The software, resources, problem order, settings and instruction are identical on every evaluation.","reason":"Score changes were measured under identical conditions."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Contradicted","quote":"No different instruction or presentation is studied.","reason":"Instruction effects were not studied."}]}],"closing_note":"Instructions were mostly clear. Ambiguities: whether 'Not established' vs 'Contradicted' applies when a passage states something was not done (I used Contradicted when explicitly stated or when the passage directly conflicts, e.g., no repeats vs 'tested repeats'); and instrument_review was applied as a brief general evidence review since no named instrument was assigned."}
